clue.text: Cunning, troublesome person departs with cape

parts.note: a shrew is a bad-tempered, nagging person
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
a ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Orford Ness

explanation.surface: Someone describes a difficult character who stormed off wearing a cloak, calling them cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape' looks like a garment beside 'troublesome person', but it is a headland: NESS appears in British place names such as Orford Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewdness and cunning are both sharp, practical cleverness, so the noun is a synonym.

clue.text: Moans about Pat losing dad's spectacles

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for moans surrounds the leftover letter

parts.note: sighs are breathy moans

indicators.note: losing tells us to take the word for dad out of Pat

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Someone complains that Pat has mislaid their father's glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectacles' looks like eyeglasses; here it means things worth seeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sights are views or scenes worth seeing, which is what spectacles are.

indicators.note: no end means the word for swelling loses its final letter

parts.note: raising, as of dough, is causing it to swell

explanation.surface: Dried produce that keeps expanding forever.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a common dried fruit.

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters are mixed up; it also suits the dog

explanation.surface: A new puppy with a duller bark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' fits the dog but means crazy, the anagram signal; 'sound' looks like a noise but means reliable.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-grounded argument is soundly based, so the adjective means valid or reliable.

clue.text: Not right upstairs, stagger going up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to stun is to stagger or astound

explanation.surface: Someone a little unhinged lurching up the staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: Not right upstairs is an idiom for mentally unsound, and crazy is what the slang adjective means.

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Regret that some American is furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanguinary means involving much bloodshed, so it is a formal synonym for bloody.

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for look in the opposite direction

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick look

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep glancing behind you.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep on, or keep going, is to continue, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: I rue Oprah broadcast, ignoring queen's happiness

indicators.note: broadcast suits a TV host but means scattered, so the letters are rearranged
ignoring means leaving out the letter for queen

parts.note: R is short for regina, queen

explanation.surface: A viewer regrets a talk-show episode, but not the queen's joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits Oprah Winfrey, the American talk-show host, but signals an anagram of I RUE OPRAH; 'ignoring queen's' then removes one R.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphoria is intense elation, an extreme form of happiness.

indicators.note: left for husband means the letter for left replaces the letter for husband

parts.note: a pheasant is a game bird

explanation.surface: A pleasing bird departed in place of a spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' could be the French city, but it is the plain adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant and nice both describe something agreeable, so they are synonyms.

parts.note: the blade of this execution machine is hoisted up before it falls; to top someone is slang for to kill them

explanation.surface: A riddle about some mechanism lifted to the highest point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like the summit the device rises to, but it is slang for execute: the blade is raised in order to top a victim.
explanation.definitionFit: The French beheading machine works by raising a heavy blade and dropping it, so it is a device raised to kill.

clue.text: Part of church collapsed? Only part

indicators.note: only part of the word collapsed is wanted, so the letters lie within it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a section of a church has fallen down, and is told only some of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church, usually holding the altar, is a part of the building.

clue.text: Regularly admits damp's turning out critical

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of admits and damp's

parts.note: proving means turning out to be, as in proving difficult

explanation.surface: Someone frequently confesses that the damp is getting worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'admits' (DIS) and of 'damp's' (AP); 'turning out' is PROVING.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing disfavour is being critical, so the adjective matches.

indicators.note: used as a verb, trousers means pockets or takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: twine is strong string or cord

explanation.surface: Corduroy trousers that are good for a sore spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cord trousers' reads as corduroy legwear, but 'trousers' is a verb meaning takes in, putting G inside TWINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinge is a sudden sharp stab of pain, so the noun is a specific kind of the defining word.

clue.text: Gold I'd returned to king, initially satisfying accountants

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: returned asks for the letters of I'd to be read backwards

parts.note: the letters of I'd, apostrophe dropped
R stands for king, from Latin rex

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of satisfying

explanation.surface: Bean counters are pleased that someone has handed gold back to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditors are accountants who inspect the financial records of a business, so they are a type of accountant.

clue.text: Partly how one makes one's mark

definitions.text: Partly how one makes one's mark

parts.words: Partly how one makes one's mark
parts.note: the possessive in the clue's own one's is formed partly by a punctuation mark, which is the answer

explanation.surface: Part of how a person achieves recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes one's mark' sounds like achieving fame; literally, the possessive one's is made partly with a raised comma.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation sign that forms a possessive is a mark used in writing words like one's.

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook brings up a police officer's payout.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid to make good a loss is a reimbursement, so the two nouns are synonyms.

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
rapping is knocking or hitting, as bashing is

explanation.surface: A grown-up performing rap music is cringeworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rapping' suggests rap music; here it means striking.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash someone is to make them ashamed, so abashing is embarrassing.

clue.text: Ray might be doing this in mum's wig, dancing with no uniform

indicators.note: dancing suggests movement, so the letters are rearranged
with no means the letter for uniform is removed

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Ray is cavorting in his mother's hairpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name; it is the flat fish, which moves through water.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray is a fish, and moving through water is what a fish does all the time.

clue.text: Things violinist might do to ingratiate themself?

definitions.meaning: a fiddler draws a ... it across the strings
the idiom for fawning, servile behaviour to win favour

explanation.surface: A question about what a fiddler might do to win favour.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase literally describes playing a violin, and idiomatically means behaving obsequiously.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting with excessive deference to curry favour, while literally naming two actions of a fiddler.

indicators.note: dismissing means the letter for female is sent out of the word

parts.note: a faction is a small dissenting group or clique

explanation.surface: A clique expelling a woman for her conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Action means conduct or what one does, so it can stand for behaviour.

explanation.surface: Something that irritates dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for pursuing someone persistently and a plural noun for hunting dogs.

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged word wraps the abbreviation
strange suggests something odd, so the letters of mystery are rearranged

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: An odd puzzle concerning a young woman's letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspondence' looks like letters, but here it means matching; a maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence in the sense of exact matching between parts is balance or symmetry.

clue.text: Cloak policeman keeps on in front of house

indicators.note: in front of places the first part before the next
keeps means holds within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: PC is a police constable

explanation.surface: An officer keeps his coat on outside a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A poncho is a blanket-like outer garment with a hole for the head, a kind of cloak.

clue.text: Very popular time to leave part of London

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: to leave means the letter for time is removed

parts.note: hot means popular or in demand

explanation.surface: A trendy moment to depart from a district of the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: SOHO is a district of central London's West End, known for nightlife, so it is part of London.

indicators.note: almost means the word for grow loses its final letter

parts.note: to rise is to grow or increase

explanation.surface: A gardener says they nearly cultivate a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a garden plant with showy blooms, an example of a flower.

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
a position is a placing or location

explanation.surface: An intern meets resentment at their work placement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work placement' reads as one phrase, an internship, but the two words are separate pieces; op is short for opus.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposition is resistance or antagonism, so hostility is a fair synonym.

clue.text: These may stop people uttering jokes

definitions.meaning: cloth bound over the mouth to stop someone speaking

explanation.surface: Remarks that are so bad they leave listeners speechless.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both mouth coverings that silence someone and comic quips.

parts.note: a longing is a strong desire or craving
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: An exhortation to want few material goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Belongings are the things a person owns, so they are possessions.
